quarterly_data.signal: Q1 FY2026 results: revenue 'came in towards the higher end of our outlook at $3.16 billion, growing 3% sequentially and 30% year-over-year', with revenue, profitability and EPS all above the midpoint of guidance and year-over-year growth broad-based, led by industrial and communications. Gross margin 71.2% (up 140 basis points sequentially and 240 basis points year-over-year on higher utilization, favorable mix and roughly 50 basis points of discrete items not in the original forecast); OpEx $812 million; operating margin 45.5%, above the high end of guidance; EPS $2.46, up 9% sequentially and 51% year-over-year. Trailing-12-month operating cash flow $5.1 billion, CapEx $0.5 billion and free cash flow $4.6 billion (39% of revenue). CEO: fiscal '26 'has the potential to be a banner year for ADI' barring unforeseen macro or geopolitical changes.
quarterly_data.figure: Rev $3.16 billion (+3% seq, +30% YoY); GM 71.2%; op margin 45.5%; EPS $2.46 (+51% YoY)

quarterly_data.signal: End-market mix Q1 FY2026: Communications was 15% of revenue, up 20% sequentially and 63% year-over-year - 'Accelerating year-over-year growth was led by our data center business as increasing investments in AI infrastructure continue to drive robust demand for our optical and power portfolios'; wireless has grown double digits for 3 consecutive quarters. Industrial was 47% of revenue (+5% sequentially, +38% year-over-year) with every segment up 25% or more and record quarters for ATE and aerospace and defense (ATE plus A&D are about 1/3 of industrial; the other 2/3 is still 20% below previous peaks). Automotive 25% of revenue (-8% sequentially, +8% year-over-year; book-to-bill ended under one after tariff-related order pull-ins; management expects auto to grow in fiscal '26). Consumer 13% (+2% sequentially, +27% year-over-year) on wearables and premium handsets. Double-digit year-over-year growth in Asia, Americas and Europe.
quarterly_data.figure: Comms 15% of revenue, +20% seq, +63% YoY (led by data center optical and power); Industrial 47%, +38% YoY

quarterly_data.signal: AI exposure sizing: ADI's automated test equipment (ATE) and data center businesses 'collectively make up close to 20% of our revenue'. CFO: 'It's over a $2 billion run rate ... About 40% of that ATE the rest is data center. And then within data center, it's pretty balanced between power and optical.' The data center business grew approximately 50% in fiscal '25 and saw accelerated growth again in Q1 FY2026; ATE revenue increased approximately 40% in fiscal '25 and further accelerated in Q1 (a record ATE quarter), with ADI supplying pin electronics, device power supplies and parametric measurement units for SoC, memory, RF and power-device test systems and content per tester 'into the tens of thousands of dollars'. ATE is expected to grow greater than 30% sequentially in Q2. CEO on growth: 'these areas will all grow at double digits over the next several years.'
quarterly_data.figure: ATE + data center close to 20% of revenue, over a $2 billion run rate (~40% ATE); data center approximately 50% growth in fiscal '25

quarterly_data.signal: Q2 FY2026 outlook: revenue $3.5 billion, plus or minus $100 million (about 11% sequential growth vs a typical 4% or 5% seasonal rise); operating margin 47.5% +/- 100 basis points at the midpoint; tax rate 11%-13%; adjusted EPS $2.88 +/- $0.15. Gross margin assumed up 100 bps reported (about 150 bps normalized) on favorable mix and price. By end market: industrial up 20% sequentially and about 50% year-over-year (ATE growing greater than 30% sequentially); communications up high single digits sequentially and about 60% year-over-year, driven by 'the AI surge for data center and the wireless cyclical recovery'; auto flat to down sequentially (tariff/macro pull-in unwind, Chinese New Year); consumer down mid-single digits. Full-year OpEx growth expected to trail revenue growth by roughly half.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 guide $3.5 billion +/- $100 million (~11% seq); op margin 47.5%; EPS $2.88; comms about 60% YoY

quarterly_data.signal: Pricing: price adjustments with channel partners took effect at the start of Q2 and ADI is 'largely through our annual negotiation with our direct customers', so Q2 should reflect the full scope of the recent pricing actions. CFO: 'about 1/3 of the quarter-over-quarter revenue increase at the midpoint is related to price. Excluding the pricing uplift, our sequential growth outlook is more like 7% versus the 11%', and roughly half of the price lift relates to one-time repricing of channel inventory that will not repeat in Q3; ADI expects 'about 50 bps of incremental growth in each of Q3 and Q4 related to price.' CEO framed the latest price increase as 'a practical response to the inflationary environment' and said ADI's innovation premium 'is extending'.
quarterly_data.figure: about 1/3 of Q2 QoQ revenue increase from price (~7% seq ex-price vs 11%); about 50 bps growth from price in each of Q3 and Q4

quarterly_data.signal: Supply and demand posture: inventory increased $111 million sequentially (days of inventory finished at 171) as ADI continues 'to build die bank and finished good buffers to help support the upside we are seeing while balancing a strategically leaner channel position'; channel inventory increased but ended within the 6- to 7-week range. Management believes customers are through the digestion phase of '24 and '25 and are 'essentially ordering to consumption', with no evidence of restocking. Industrial book-to-bill was 'well above 1' excluding pricing, with positive book-to-bill across all industrial sectors and geographies; ATE and aerospace and defense are 'continuing to achieve new highs' and, 'given that momentum in bookings and backlog, we don't see this trend stopping'; auto book-to-bill ended under one. ADI expects fiscal 2026 CapEx within its long-term model of 4% to 6% of revenue.
quarterly_data.figure: Inventory +$111 million QoQ; channel within 6- to 7-week range; industrial book-to-bill well above 1; fiscal 2026 CapEx 4% to 6% of revenue

players.product: grid-to-chip power - grid monitoring & BMS, 800V-to-intermediate conversion, intermediate-to-core rails and Empower IVR vertical power delivery

quarterly_data.signal: Data center power franchise breakdown: 'ADI's hot swap and high-performance protection solutions which represent roughly 1/3 of our data center power revenue today' enable fault isolation, fast recovery and live maintenance as customers migrate to higher-voltage architectures; 'Roughly 1/3 of our data center power revenue comes from DC power control, including our power system management ICs and multiphase controllers.' Strong growth continues in point-of-load converters, micro modules and high-performance regulators, and 'new approaches such as vertical power and higher voltage distribution, are now opening incremental SAM for ADI.' ADI 'shipped our smart power stage to our first vertical power customer last quarter, and adoption of our intermediate bus converter modules is accelerating for 48- and 54-volt architectures.' CEO: power systems are becoming more digitally controlled (multiphase, very high-speed conversion managing more rails), and 'computing performance equals availability of power'.
quarterly_data.figure: Hot swap/protection roughly 1/3 of DC power revenue; DC power control roughly 1/3; first vertical power customer shipped; IBC modules for 48- and 54-volt

players.product: optical CONTROL path - timing, power management, data conversion, monitoring & control for lasers/transceivers, OCS and CPO

quarterly_data.signal: Optical connectivity: as AI data movement grows exponentially, 'industry leaders are re-architecting their networks, increasingly replacing traditional electrical switching with Optical Circuit Switches or OCS.' Performance 'increasingly depends on the precision control monitoring and power solutions, the nervous system, if you will, around the laser, DSP and photodiode signal chain' - ADI integrates precision control, temperature regulation, real-time monitoring and compact power management so optical systems run at higher speeds with lower power in smaller form factors, raising front-panel bandwidth density and cutting cost per bit. The optical 'nervous system' mixes digital functionality with ADI's mixed-signal conversion and power. Data center revenue is 'pretty balanced between power and optical', and Q1 communications growth was led by data center demand for ADI's optical and power portfolios.
quarterly_data.figure: no specific figure (data center revenue pretty balanced between power and optical)
